title: Estimation and Approximation: Decimal Places and Significant Figures
seo_title: Estimation and Approximation – JSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Round numbers to the nearest whole number, ten, hundred and thousand; approximate to decimal places and significant figures; estimate answers. (summary of the NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 maths worksheets on rounding, decimal places, significant figures and estimating calculations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Look at the next digit: 5 or more, round up
key_sub: Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To round to 2 decimal places, look at the third decimal digit.
  • Significant figures are counted from the first non-zero digit: 0.004 72 to 2 s.f. is 0.0047.
  • To estimate, round each number to 1 significant figure and work it out.

Examples

Example

3.8462 to 2 d.p.

Next digit 6

Answer: 3.85

Example

48,617 to 2 s.f.

Next digit 6

Answer: 49,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dropping zeros that hold place48,617 to 2 s.f. is 49,000, not 49.
Counting leading zeros as significantIn 0.0047 the zeros are not significant.
Rounding twiceLook only at the next digit.

faq.a: To make numbers simpler and to check answers.
Yes, between or after non-zero digits in a measured value.
